items.title: Verstappen wins; McLaren secure a double podium
items.summary: Verstappen beat Norris by 0.639 seconds and Piastri by 1.529. Mercedes had contested the lead, but Russell fell to ninth late and Antonelli to fourth.
items.why_it_matters: Use the official result and keep the late Mercedes drop specific to Las Vegas rather than treating it as a Qatar forecast.

sources.label: Formula1.com race report, full article checked

items.title: Leclerc and Hamilton address the Las Vegas fallout
items.summary: After a Turn 7 collision, Leclerc accepted blame; team principal Fred Vasseur called it 'unacceptable' and 'a lack of respect', two races after another clash in Mexico. Formula1.com's reports differ on whether it was Lap 37 or Lap 38, so no lap number is given. Formula1.com confirms Hamilton finished seventh after serving his separate 10-second penalty; the final classification is consistent with the served sanction. At Qatar media day on 26 November, Hamilton said Ferrari's priority is securing second in the Constructors' Championship, the drivers remain free to race, and process/communication improvements will be discussed over winter. This reports ongoing conversations, not a new team rule.
items.why_it_matters: Keep Leclerc's 10-second final-result penalty separate from Hamilton's 10-second penalty served during the race. Hamilton's comments describe Ferrari's current target and future discussions; they announce no new team rules and do not predict the next race.

items.title: Perez has a five-place drop at his next race
items.summary: The stewards found Perez wholly responsible for contact with Câmara at Turn 14. Because Perez retired, the unserved time penalty was converted to a five-place drop at his next race.
items.why_it_matters: Qatar is the expected next application. This is a grid penalty, not a five-second race penalty, and the Vegas PU sanctions must not be carried over a second time.

items.title: Hadjar's front wing fails; a separate Safety Car penalty demotes him
items.summary: Hadjar reached the lead battle before his front wing collapsed; he said he did not know the cause. A separate 10-second penalty for driving unnecessarily slowly behind the Safety Car dropped him to 15th.
items.why_it_matters: Keep the wing-failure cause unconfirmed and distinguish it from the Safety Car infringement.

items.title: Mercedes adds a reported software safeguard after Antonelli's battery loss
items.summary: Mercedes team principal Toto Wolff said Antonelli lifted behind Verstappen before reapplying, leaving him with no battery on the back straight; both McLarens passed and Antonelli finished fourth. Wolff said Mercedes had planned an energy deployment for the final 400 metres that could have offered a chance to win. The Race's 26 November Qatar report says Antonelli described a safety feature Mercedes added to make the energy-management system more robust after that loss.
items.why_it_matters: Attribute the race account to Wolff and the software change to The Race's report of Antonelli's comments, not independent telemetry. The team-side change is not an FIA energy-limit revision, and its effect at Qatar is not yet demonstrated.

sources.label: The Race, Qatar day-one report quoting Antonelli, 26 November
